rationale: The entry's unifying core (a generative word or life planted to reproduce after its kind) accounts for every cited text without remainder: Gen 1 supplies the 'after his kind' mechanics; the sower texts identify seed as word; Matt 13:38 identifies good seed as children; Gen 3:15/Gal 3:16 identify the promised Seed as Messiah; and Isa 51:2 plus the mustard-seed/tree texts show one planted life expanding into house/people/nation-tree. No supplied detail requires a narrower single-track primary. The strongest counters (word-primary or Messiah-primary) each leave half the printed references unexplained or secondary, whereas the entry's generative frame covers all of them as instances of the same reproductive pattern.
book_core_identification: Seed is a generative word or life planted so as to reproduce after its kind.
book_secondary_elaborations: In the sower it is God's word
In the wheat and tares it is children
One planted person may grow into a house, people, or nation-tree
chapter_only_objections: Chapter-level claims that every parable element (ground, thorns, fowls, leaven, treasure, pearl, net) must be derived solely from OT patterns before any NT key is consulted
Chapter-level inversion of the treasure and pearl parables (people as treasure/pearl, Christ as buyer) and negative reading of leaven
Extended tree/grass/mountain/beast nation-scale system and clean/unclean diet permanence beyond the seed entry itself
strongest_counter_interpretation: Seed's primary and authoritative symbolic meaning is the word/gospel of God sown into hearts (explicitly defined by Jesus in the sower), with offspring/Messiah, children-of-the-kingdom, death-resurrection, and growth-from-small-beginnings as legitimate but secondary, context-bound uses.
counter_core_identification: Seed primarily symbolizes the word of God / gospel message.
material_core_denial: The counter does not deny that seed can be generative life or Messiah; it simply ranks word-of-God as the single primary sense and treats the other printed applications as non-core.
counter_case: Luke 8:11 / Mark 4:14 / Matt 13:19 supply an explicit dominical definition ('the seed is the word') that the entry demotes to one instance among equals
Mainstream teaching and the bulk of parabolic/devotional usage treat the sower as the controlling symbol
Offspring and Messiah senses are real but belong to a different (covenantal) register and need not be collapsed into the same glossary headword
book_explanatory_advantages: Single generative frame simultaneously covers Gen 1 'after his kind', sower-word, tares-children, promised-Seed-Messiah, and mustard-to-nation-tree without ranking any as secondary
Isa 51:2 and John 12:24 fit naturally as life-planted-and-multiplied rather than as exceptions to a word-only core
Preserves the explicit NT keys (Matt 13:38; Gal 3:16) as coordinate rather than subordinate
counter_explanatory_advantages: Privileges the one place Jesus himself supplies an on-the-spot definition
Matches the most common pastoral and catechetical usage of 'seed'
decisive_sources: Matt 13:19 + 13:38 (word and children in adjacent kingdom parables)
Isa 51:2 + Matt 13:31-32 (one planted life becomes nation-tree)
